item.title: Re: Suggestions?
item.content:encoded:
The janitor closet isn't the bad thing by itself, it is just that the extreme measures taken to contain the item didn't really fit into the idea of the item being outside the Foundation'n reach.

I think you could explore both aspects very well, but not at the same time: the measures to keep it from touching anything, or the procedures for effective containment outside a facility and behind enemy lines.

item.title: Re: Suggestions?
item.content:encoded:
A thought I just thought up: what if this was the first SCP where the Foundation had interaction with the Church of the Broken God?

AFAIK, 882 doesn't explicitly mention the CotBG at all, and this is one of the first articles that involved it. What I'm thinking is: the Foundation finds SCP-271 in some Ancient Egyptian temple, or something, and makes note of "religious markings matching those of no known religion." Then the Foundation gets a letter from the "Church of the Broken God," telling us about how they want SCP-882, SCP-217, and SCP-271 back, because they're important religious artifacts. The Foundation tells them to eff off.

Then they raid Site-19, or whatever. We see them as half-men and half-machine, nearly unstoppable, but we repel them, but they manage to make off with SCP-271. We send an agent/an MTF into their compound to get it back. There's a lot of worldbuilding with the Broken God that could be done there, and we can see how they were planning to use SCP-271. We get it back, and we lock it up.

Thoughts?

item.title: Re: Suggestions?
item.content:encoded:
Done! :) I'm toying with the idea that the reason the 001 proposal didn't work properly was because its heart was a Factory-made replacement for 271 (which lacks any obvious clockwork accoutrements, so Bumaro had a completely different idea of what he was looking for).

I don't think the Foundation would be able to separate 271 from 882 if they came into contact - the disk would be incorporated into the clockworks, and the script would spread to the rest of the gears, turning them into adamantium as well (and since adamantium doesn't rust, 882+271 would no longer be contained). I do want to emphasise how elegantly they fit together, but I think it would have to be done by figuring out the origin of the language.

The unique security situation is the weakest idea I had, and it's at odds with what I'm thinking about for the object's history now anyway. Maybe for some other SCP.

If you haven't already, I'd recommend reading the TGDK 001 proposal, as it actually deals with the idea of all of these anomalies coming together to form the Broken God.

Some suggestions, in response to your points:

  • If you want it to be a god language, say it's a god language. Maybe add an addendum about a study finding similarities to the language on SCP-271 and the language on some CotBG ruins somewhere.
  • If you want to emphasize the components part, maybe have an incident log where 271 comes in contact with 882?

item.title: Re: Suggestions?
item.content:encoded:
Hello, and welcome back!
There's no problem if your depiction of the CotBG is contrary to the usually accepted one. SCP-1461 and The Worm tale already give an alternate origin for it that's more suitable for straight horror. Even without considering that, the Sic Semper Tyrannis tale already states this and several other Church articles were corrupted to use as weapons.
As for this being a perfect ur-language and a fragment of God's brain, there are two SCPs that work with a "Broken language" already (SCP-1139 and SCP-2660), and one that has a blueprint for it's mind (SCP-635, as depicted in the Broken Mind tale) so you could read those and figure out in which direction you want to take this.
If you want a TL;DR of each article (don't, they're all great), I'm leaving them below:

Open
- Close
  • SCP-1461 and The Worm: The Church started because of a WW1 soldier who had a vision of a worm consuming everything and of machines he could build to trap it. He ends up realizing he actually gave it more power that way, that the visions came from the worm. It's ambiguous if the Womr ever existed or if it was the soldier and then the cultists just going insane. The article ends with the following recording: I am the trap. I am the trapped./I am beauty and I am chaos./Children are selfish./I am the worm./I have broken God.
  • Sic Semper Tyrannis: The ancient Mekhanite Empire lost their war against the Sarkics and, in a desperate last resort, corrupted their most sacred artifacts so that when Grand Karcist Ion tried to consume them, he ended up destroying himself.
  • SCP-1139: Basically the tower of Babel, changing people's languages into incomprehensible new ones when activated, and making them unable to ever learn other ones.
  • SCP-2660: A lamp that got bonded with the Broken God's Signal and has made it impossible to hide or lie about it, as well as about anything it is illuminating. It's implied it has further effects with long-term exposure.
  • SCP-635: A book that compels people to read it and build machines. Those machines then build more complex machines, and the cycle continues indefinitely. The Broken Mind tale states this is a set of instructions to reconstruct the Broken God's mind.

item.title: Re: Suggestions?
item.content:encoded: Hello! It's always nice to see older authors come back to the wiki. Welcome back, I suppose. As you noted, the article hasn't exactly aged well. I think it could be heavily improved by simply updating the clinical tone and redactions and whatnot to the standards of a modern day article. Cleaning up and redoing the connection to the Church and making them more well-defined is a solid idea. The concept is fun to play around with, and I think that adding more content regarding the relationship between 271, 217, and 882 could definitely help the article, considering that's what it was meant to be all along. There seems to be a lot of untapped potential with the language idea, that could definitely less in an interesting direction if you took it there and had the Foundation look into it. I agree that you should probably redo the containment procedures, especially with the slightly bizarre janitor closet. If you'd like to look at some newer CotBG articles, I'd highly recommend the 001 proposal and SCP-2217. I'd love to offer more help if you're up for it!

item.title: Suggestions?
item.content:encoded:
Hey. So. Umm.

It's been most of a decade since I've been an active writer here, but I'm kind of interested in coming back. I'd like to revise and update this article - as people have mentioned in the comments, it has aged extremely poorly, and the fact that the Foundation and the CotBG have since been more defined and pinned down contrary to the way I depicted them doesn't help either.

I'm a little lost as to where to start, though - the Foundation has become so huge that I'm not sure exactly how to catch up on everything.

  • My original intent is that the fractal inscriptions on SCP-271 are like the Broken God's version of Enochian - the perfect ur-language which describes the God's thoughts. This language was destroyed when the God was broken; this fragment of adamantium comprises all that remains of its mind, comparable to a single neuron of the the God's brain.
  • 217, 271, and 882 were meant to be the key components of the Broken God. 217 turns living things into organic clockwork, 271 turns everything into metal, 882 grows by absorbing metal. Bringing them together would have disastrous consequences, not because of some shared mystical connection, but because they function synergistically and eliminate each others' limitations. The three combined would create a clockwork Grey Goo scenario which would transform the Earth into the Repaired God.
  • The idea of field containment procedures for SCPs which have yet to be moved to a secure site still interests me, but everything here related to it is just embarassingly gimmicky and I probably might as well throw it all out.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I know this is a very old article so this might not matter to most, but the fact that it uses the Phaistos Disc as the picture is very disruptive for me. I read this one a long time ago and again today and it brings me right out of the article (outside of that, i'm neutral on whether it's a good SCP or not).

The thing is, the disc is a real archaeological object that we're taught in school about (I've actually seen it in the museum and school books use the exact same image) and the article makes no reference to that fact. I'd propose these solutions:

1. Acknowledge that there is a clay duplicate that has been planted by Foundation personnel, that have also fabricated the information currently known about it (the wikipedia article does mention that some dispute it's authenticity as an artifact).

2. Acknowledge that the real disc is quite similar or identical to the object but made of clay and of unknown relationship to the one described in the article.

3. Use a modification of the disc image or use a different image outright, since the article does not depend on the disc being specifically the Phaistos Disc but simply a disc of unknown material with weird pictographic symbols on it.

I have some minor other points to comment on: there doesn't seem to be a reason to contain it in a glass sphere, why doesn't the disc contaminate the pedestal it is touching (and if it is, why doesn't the pedestal contaminate the glass it's touching - the article says the symbols can't penetrate non-gaseous fluids, but two solid objects in contact might be close enough to have less than total coverage along their contact surfaces) and there seems to be little indication of why the disc is indestructible (and how the foundation knows that) when the contaminated materials are destructible even though they're composed of the same unknown metallic material.

Also, the proper term for something turning into metal is, I think, crystallization and not petrification (as the latter refers to something turning into stone, while metals are crystalline in nature, afaik) - but now I'm just nitpicking :P

But maybe it's Keter because of what the Chruch might do with it? Classification has to do with the level of resources required to contain the item as well as the consequences of containment failure. I have three reasons why that is a bad idea.

First question: has that ever actually worked?

Second question: are you certain of the consequences of turning, for example, Mars, into an anomalous metal with unknown properties? And wouldn't that be rather masquerade-breaking for the Foundation if it happened?

Third question: given that we don't actually have complete control over this object at the moment, do you have a plan to get it safely and completely out of CBG hands and into Site 19, without risking a containment breach at any stage and exposing any number of currently Safe and Euclid SCPs to a Keter-class object? Especially considering that the Church is actively tracking this object and the location of Site 19 is a closely-guarded secret?
